haiku-low.q1: MySQL first: the write, re-read and outbox row commit together on MySQL. Then one Postgres copy is tried with a 250 ms timeout. If Postgres fails, the caller still gets success; the outbox row stays for the sweeper.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the copy inserts a missing row, or the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version. Equal or higher versions are never overwritten.
haiku-low.q3: dual_write_all_since must be set and the live flag must be mysql_dual, with every expected instance reporting it. Instances can disagree on flags for up to 30 seconds.
haiku-low.q4: It reads the MySQL replica in batches of 2000 and pauses while replica lag is above 5 seconds or missing, checking every 5 seconds before each batch.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: compare_clean_at under 24 hours old, then the 1/10/50/100 ramp, each level held 1 hour with good Postgres health. Source-of-truth move: 3 days at 100% reads, clean recent comparison, empty outbox, users_id_seq present, staging rollback drill passed.
haiku-low.q6: The users_sync_outbox row on the source-of-truth database, written in the same transaction as the write. The sweeper retries the copy until it succeeds, with backoff capped at 60 seconds.
haiku-low.q7: Postgres: a trigger takes an advisory lock on the id and skips writes when a tombstone exists; erasure takes the same lock. MySQL: copies check the tombstone with SELECT FOR SHARE. Tombstones are kept permanently.
haiku-low.q8: In last_completed_id in the Postgres migration_state table, updated in the same transaction as each batch upsert, so both or neither persist. It stops when a batch returns zero rows, then writes backfill_complete_at.
haiku-low.q9: The comparison job: two keyset walks check every row on both sides. Persistent mismatches get an outbox row queued for repair and the pass is not clean. A clean pass writes compare_clean_at.
haiku-low.q10: The switch sets the old side's control row to moving; writes hold FOR SHARE on it, so new writes block and get 503s. If the drain exceeds 40 seconds, the script restores sot. Abort is allowed only before step 4.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres users_id_seq assigns ids after the switch, set to GREATEST(current, MySQL MAX(id)) + 1,000,000. The reverse copy passes ids explicitly. On rollback MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set to MAX(id)+1, and later sequences take the larger side.
haiku-low.q12: Reverse dual writes (inline copy plus sweeper) keep MySQL current during the 14-day soak. Rollback fences Postgres, drains its outbox, sets MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, flips control rows and the flag. The option ends at Step 10, pg_only.

sonnet.q1: MySQL (the SoT) is written first, in one transaction that also inserts an outbox row. After commit, a single inline copy to Postgres is attempted with a 250 ms timeout. If Postgres fails, the caller still sees success; the failure is logged and a metric bumped.
sonnet.q2: Only if the row is missing (insert), or the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version (version rule). Also tombstoned (erased) users are never written.
sonnet.q3: dual_write_all_since must be set: app_flag_value{flag="users.write_mode"} shows mysql_dual on every expected instance, plus 60 more seconds of waiting, and the live flag must still be mysql_dual. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds (flags cached, refreshed every 30 s).
sonnet.q4: It reads in batches of 2000 rows from the MySQL replica (not the primary), checking before each batch (every 5 s) and pausing while mysql_replica_lag_seconds is above 5 or missing; it resumes by itself.
sonnet.q5: Reads: backfill_complete_at is set, the oldest outbox row is under 1 minute old, and a clean full comparison (compare_clean_at) is under 24 hours old; then ramp 1, 10, 50, 100% holding each at least 1 hour with good Postgres error rate and p99. Source of truth move (Step 8): reads at 100% for at least 3 days, last comparison clean and under 24 hours old, outbox empty, users_id_seq exists, and a rollback drill has passed in staging.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (users_sync_outbox), written in the same transaction as the write, on the SoT (MySQL) database. The sweeper (standalone worker, retries forever with backoff capped at 60 s) re-reads the user and applies the copy to Postgres under the version rule, then deletes the outbox row.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones in users_tombstone (on both DBs, permanent). Postgres: a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(NEW.id) and skips the write if a tombstone exists; the delete path takes the same lock before inserting the tombstone. MySQL: copies first run SELECT 1 FROM users_tombstone WHERE id=? FOR SHARE, which gap-locks the absent key so a concurrent tombstone insert waits. The sweeper also writes a tombstone if the source row is absent.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres table migration_state (last_completed_id). It is updated in the same Postgres transaction as the batch upsert, so both or neither happen; repeated batches are harmless under the version rule. It stops when a batch returns zero rows, then writes backfill_complete_at.
sonnet.q9: The full comparison job (Step 5, nightly after reads move). It does two keyset walks (SoT ids checked on the other side; other side's ids checked on SoT) of 10,000 ids, comparing all columns, re-checking candidates 30 s later. Persistent mismatches with no pending outbox row get an outbox row queued (repair by the sweeper) and the pass is not clean; a pass with zero persistent mismatches writes compare_clean_at. A recurring same mismatch means stop and diagnose the dual-write code.
sonnet.q10: A control row (users_control.state: sot/moving/not_sot) on each DB; every SoT-first write takes FOR SHARE on its side's control row and returns a retryable 503 unless state is sot. The switcher's UPDATE to moving waits for in-flight writes, then blocks all new ones, so stale-flag instances get 503s and never write to the wrong side. If step 2 (drain of outbox) is not done within 40 seconds, the script sets the old side back to sot (abort, allowed only before step 4); writes resume and leftover outbox rows go to the sweeper. Worst case is about 70 seconds against the 90 second limit.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids via users_id_seq, which at the switch is set to GREATEST(current, MAX(id) on MySQL primary) + 1,000,000; the reverse copy passes the ids explicitly to MySQL. On rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set to MAX(id)+1, and on any later switch the sequence takes the larger of both sides so it never goes backwards.
sonnet.q12: Step 9 reverse dual writes: Postgres is SoT, and MySQL is kept current by the inline copy plus the sweeper (outbox on Postgres), with nightly comparison. Rollback is the mirror of Step 8: fence Postgres, drain the Postgres outbox, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to MAX(id)+1, set MySQL sot and Postgres not_sot, set the flag to mysql_dual, with the same 40 s abort rule. Reads may stay on Postgres. The option ends at Step 10 (write_mode=pg_only, after at least 14 days, outbox empty, clean comparison), the point of no return; reverting to pg_dual is then possible but needs a Postgres-to-MySQL comparison and repair first.
